timeline.what: v2.4 released to all traffic; offline evaluation passed on an English-only set
Arabic quality burn-rate alert pages on-call
rollback to v2.3; Arabic answers recover
breach assessed with the data protection officer: harm likely
SDAIA notified; affected customers told by text message

contributing_factors.factor: The offline evaluation set had no Arabic tracking questions and no Eastern Arabic digits
contributing_factors.evidence: evaluation_set_arabic_share 0.0; release engineer's note at minute 30

contributing_factors.factor: The v2.4 prompt template dropped the digit normalisation step
contributing_factors.evidence: model platform's note at minute 41; all twelve failing cases use Eastern Arabic digits

contributing_factors.factor: The tracking lookup falls back to the nearest parcel number instead of refusing
contributing_factors.evidence: finding at minute 32; answers named parcels the customer did not ask about

contributing_factors.factor: The release went to all traffic at once, with no canary and no quality gate
The on-call engineer had no written authority to roll back without the evaluation team
